title: Impact Path
description: The ordered chain of entities and typed relationships connecting a changed entity to an affected one. The path is what makes an impact finding auditable: a consumer can walk the steps and check each relationship against its evidence, which is impossible from a hop count alone. Steps are typed so that a path is never merely a list of nodes with an implied sequence.

nodes.description: The entities along the path, starting at the changed entity and ending at the affected entity. Must contain exactly one more entry than steps, which rule impact/transitive-impact enforces because JSON Schema cannot express the relationship between two array lengths.

steps.description: The typed relationships between consecutive nodes.

hopDepth.description: The number of steps. Equal to the length of steps.

direction.description: Which way the change propagated along this path.

termination.description: Why the path stops where it does. Recorded so that a bounded traversal is not mistaken for an exhausted one.

confidence.description: The aggregated confidence for the whole path, computed as the minimum ordinal across the steps.

step.description: One traversed relationship within a path.

source.description: The entity the step starts at.

target.description: The entity the step ends at.

relationship.description: The relationship traversed. Constrained to relationship-types, whose changePropagation decides whether this step propagates a change forward, backward, or not at all.

edgeId.description: The dependency edge this step corresponds to, when the step came from an edge in the analysed graph.

direction.description: Whether the change propagated with the arrow or against it at this step. Required, because the same relationship can be traversed either way and the two mean different things.

evidence.description: Evidence for this step. Rule impact/transitive-impact requires evidence on every step, not only on the finding as a whole, because a path is only as supported as its weakest link.
